  COVID- 19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
  Due to the existing COVID - 19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City Council Meeting of December 14, 2021, at 2:00 p.m. (Or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments:Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, City Clerk staff will check and print emails prior to arriving in the Council Chambers. In the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310- 412 - 5280 with any questions.

  2.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  >  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.

  > Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

  > The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.

  3.  Members of the public who wish to address the City Council orally must use the public access option noted below:

  l

  December 14, 2021 –Access Code: 9507848#

Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability - related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412 - 5280, FAX at 310 -412 - 5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  December 14, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
December 14, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers at the hour of 2:02 p.m.

Mayor Butts congratulated Council Woman Faulk and City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson,
on their one-year of service.

The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman / Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking
  Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman
  Butts,  Council  Members/Successor  Agency
  Members/Housing  Authority  Members/  Finance
  Authority Members/ Parking Authority Members/Joint
  Powers Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Finance Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint
Powers officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on
the Agendas.

Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 5,6,11, 10, DR-1, and DR-4.

Ray Howler commented on Agenda Item Nos. O-1, Adoption of the two (2) Ordinances
(Ordinance Nos. 22-02 and 22-03) associated with the Westchester/Veterans and
Crenshaw/Imperial Transit Oriented Development Plan and Design Guidelines, 5,
Approving an Advanced Funds Agreement between the City of Inglewood and 225 N. La
Brea, LLC.

Dana Bowl, Los Angeles County of Public Defenders commented on Agenda Item No.
10, Adoption of a resolution authorizing the destruction of specified Police Department
Records.

Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised
to call back towards the end of the meeting to address his concerns.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Dotson, and seconded by

  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated

  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,

  1. Daryl Alexander for alleged property damage; tree roots encroachment on July 29,
  2021.
  2. Corine Andrewin for alleged vehicle tow and storage on October 9, 2021.
  3. Jazmin Ramirez for alleged discrimination, HWE, wrongful termination,
  discriminatory conduct and retaliation in February 2020.
  B. Return Late Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 911.2:

183  PUBLIC HEARING SET – TO DETERMINE IF THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR PROJECT (ITC) IS EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) UNDER PUBLIC RESOURCES
  CODE SECTION 21080, SUBDIVISION (B)(12), AND CALIFORNIA CODE OF
  REGULATIONS, TITLE 14 (“STATE CEQA GUIDELINES”) SECTION 15275,
  SUBDIVISON (B), AS A “FACILITY EXTENSION NOT TO EXCEED FOUR (4)
  MILES IN LENGTH, WHICH [IS] REQUIRED FOR THE TRANSFER OF
  PASSENGERS FROM OR THE EXCLUSIVE PUBLIC MASS TRANSIT
  GUIDEWAY OR BUSWAY PUBLIC TRANSIST SERVICES.” Staff report dated
  December 14, 2021, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to receive
  public comments to determine if the Inglewood Transit Connector Project (ITC) is
  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Public Resources
  Code section 21080, subdivision (b)(12), and California Code of Regulations, Title 14
  (“State CEQA Guidelines”) section 15275, subdivision (b), as a “facility extension not to
  exceed four (4) miles in length, which [is] required for the transfer of passengers from or
  to exclusive public mass transit guideway or busway public transit services.”

  Lisa Trifiletti presented the City Council with an update on the project, reporting on the
  recirculated draft of the Environmental Impact Report (EIR) on November 12, 2021, and
  the close of the comment period will conclude on December 27, 2021. She mentioned
  they plan to continue the process and bring forth the final EIR, the associated
  entitlements, and the exemption. She also reported that the Inglewood Transit Connector
  (ITC) Project is exempt as a transit facility extension. Progress is being made in working
  with the Federal Transportation Administration (FTA) to seek federal funding. She
  further stated that the FTA wanted to ensure that they conducted an environmental
  assessment as the ITC Project moves forward under the National Environmental Policy
  Act (NEPA), under California law but at the Federal level.
  Additionally, she stated that a study is required to ensure no significant impacts and the
  appropriate mitigations are made. She also stated that several other versions of the
  automated people mover were studied, including using At-Grade, but this caused
  concerns about loss of capacity on the roadways and more disruptions in the local
  communities. Finally, she added that the FTA hoped the City Council would approve the
  project as a locally preferred alternative that would allow them to continue to study the
  project.
  Mayor Butts left the dais at the hour of 2:26 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at the hour of 2:27 p.m.
